instances.text: Learnable Multipliers (LRM) [cite] address this limitation by attaching learnable scalar or vector multipliers to weight matrices, allowing scale to be learned from data while the base weights remain bounded by weight decay.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: A practical complication arises when LRM is applied to the query (Q) and key (K) projections in multi-head attention [cite].
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: More recently, Velikanov et al. [cite] proposed Learnable Multipliers (LRM), which attach learnable scalar multipliers to weight matrices in transformers, allowing the model to learn optimal scales that escape the weight decay equilibrium norm.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: Stock et al. [cite] introduced equi-normalization (ENorm), an iterative algorithm that balances weight norms across layers without changing the network function.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: Saul [cite] provided a theoretical framework for weight-balancing, showing how to derive flows that maintain minimal regularizer values during optimization.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: Terin [cite] formalized these symmetries as gauge redundancies and introduced soft gauge-fixing penalties that stabilize training by suppressing scale drift.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: For transformers specifically, Wang & Wang [cite] characterized the complete gauge group structure, proving that multi-head attention admits (GL(dk))h ×(GL(dv))h symmetries that persist through LayerNorm.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.

instances.text: In the context of LRM, Velikanov et al. [cite] found that light weight decay (λ = 2×10−3) on multipliers effectively controls symmetry-induced drift.
instances.why: Cites one work and relates it to nothing else.
